stem: A kidney recipient on sirolimus reports new lipid panel abnormalities. Which adverse effect aligns with standard medication references?

options.text: Permanent elimination of all cholesterol production
Guaranteed improvement in lipid levels compared with all other immunosuppressants
Lipid changes that never occur with proliferation signal inhibitors

explanation.rationale_correct: Common adverse effects of sirolimus and everolimus include hyperlipidemia, along with hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertriglyceridemia.

rationale_incorrect.B: Sirolimus is associated with elevated lipids rather than eliminating cholesterol production.
rationale_incorrect.C: Hyperlipidemia is a recognized side effect rather than guaranteed lipid improvement.
rationale_incorrect.D: Hyperlipidemia is among the most common proliferation signal inhibitor side effects.

stem: A solid-organ transplant recipient develops progressive neurological deficits months after transplant without fever or nuchal rigidity. Which infectious complication should the coordinator include in the differential?

options.text: Hyperacute cellular rejection presenting as isolated meningismus
Expected benign postoperative change requiring no evaluation
Oral aversion as the primary cause of progressive neurologic decline

explanation.rationale_correct: JC virus causes progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy with progressive neurological deficits; it is a noninflammatory CNS infection not associated with fever or meningeal signs and may present months to years after transplant.

rationale_incorrect.B: PML is described as noninflammatory without fever or meningeal signs rather than hyperacute rejection with meningismus.
rationale_incorrect.C: Progressive neurological deficits warrant evaluation for opportunistic infections such as PML.
rationale_incorrect.D: Oral aversion is an intestinal feeding complication unrelated to progressive CNS demyelination.

stem: A kidney recipient is starting sirolimus maintenance therapy. Evaluate the following medication-safety statements:

elements.text: Hyperlipidemia is among the common adverse effects of sirolimus and everolimus.
Sirolimus and everolimus may be associated with pneumonitis.
Sirolimus is routinely recommended without restriction for all liver transplant recipients.
Routine sirolimus trough level monitoring is recommended.

explanation.rationale_correct: Sirolimus and everolimus commonly cause hyperlipidemia and may cause pneumonitis; routine trough monitoring is recommended. Statement III is false because sirolimus has a black box warning against use in liver transplantation due to hepatic artery thrombosis risk.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also correct—routine sirolimus trough monitoring is recommended.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statements I and II are also true; statement III is false for liver transplantation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false—sirolimus is not routinely recommended for all liver recipients.

stem: The family of a 4-year-old kidney transplant recipient calls reporting sudden anuria. How should the coordinator classify this finding?

options.text: An urgent graft complication such as arterial thrombosis requiring immediate team contact
A non-urgent finding that may wait until the next routine refill call
Expected benign postoperative diuresis requiring no notification
A reason to permanently stop immunosuppression without medical guidance

explanation.rationale_correct: In pediatric kidney recipients, arterial thrombosis presents with sudden anuria and is often irreversible, resulting in graft loss; sudden anuria warrants urgent transplant team evaluation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Sudden anuria after pediatric kidney transplant is an urgent graft concern, not a routine matter.
rationale_incorrect.C: Anuria reflects possible vascular thrombosis rather than expected benign diuresis.
rationale_incorrect.D: Urgent symptoms require team contact and evaluation rather than unilateral immunosuppression cessation.
